thread:
olivia-cs: Hey team — Juno reported a bunch of 429s and tail latency spikes this morning on their dedicated pool 'pyxis'. They say baseline QPS ~220, peaked at ~1.1k for ~6m, and saw timeouts + 429s. Can we triage?

mike-eng: Thanks — do we have their pool config and autoscale policy? Also need recent POD logs and any throttle events.

olivia-cs: Pool config: reserved 12xA100 slots, autoscale min=6 max=24, target_utilization=0.65. Customer attached graphs and we saw sustained utilization hitting 92% during peak. They were on model rwd-3b-quant.

sara-sre: I'm pulling infra events. Seeing a burst of queueing around 2076543000-2076543360. Autoscaler triggered two times but both scaled by +2 only — scaling cadence seems slow relative to surge. Noisy-tenant signals: one tenant (internal 'atlas') had a long-running batch job around same time. Could be noisy neighbor.

lina-telemetry: Adding telemetry: per-tenant QPS breakdown shows Juno at baseline 220, spike to 1100 for 5m, atlas had a concurrent spike of ~800 QPS with many long responses (avg latency 1.8s). KV cache hit rate for Juno dropped 40% during the surge (cache eviction or prefix mismatch?).

mike-eng: If atlas held long-running KV cache slots, that could reduce effective serving throughput for Juno. Also rwd-3b-quant on A100 might be memory-bound when KV cache grows. Can we repro with a small script?

kevin-ml: Suggest repro steps: 1) Run sustained qps to Juno tenant: `while true; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/predict -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-3b-quant\",\"input\":\"lorem\"}'; sleep 0.06; done` 2) Simultaneously run batch-style long seqs from atlas tenant to simulate KV pressure.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] scale_event: pool=pyxis, from=8, to=10, trigger=utilization>0.8, ts=2076543142

ops-bot: [throttle] 429_event: pool=pyxis, tenant=juno, count=134, window=5m, ts=2076543301

mike-eng: Good. Lina, can you pull pod-level p95/p99 latencies and per-pod GPU utilization during the window? I want to know if slow nodes or stragglers caused descheduling.

lina-telemetry: Pulled. One pod (pyxis-pod-7) p99 requests = 4.2s, GPU util ~98% and memory coming close to 95% — likely KV overflow. Other pods stable p99 ~1.2s. NTP skew? no. Pod 7 also shows elevated context-switch counts.

sara-sre: That pod also shows a few OOM kills earlier last week — possible degraded worker. Recommend cordon+replace to rule out node-level issues.

mike-eng: Action plan: 1) Replace pod-7 (cordon + recreate) 2) Temporarily increase max autoscale to 32 for pyxis and reduce target_utilization to 0.55 to give headroom for customer peaks 3) Add per-tenant throttle ramp to protect baseline (cap bursts above 400 qps to soft-queue) 4) Run repro script with atlas batch to validate isolation 5) Follow up with Juno on warmup recommendations for their traffic pattern.

olivia-cs: Noted. I'll ask Juno to run warmup and provide exact client QPS schedule. Also will request permission to temporarily increase capacity.

kevin-ml: Also add a rule to the cache manager to favor short-lived prompts for smaller tenants; reduces eviction churn. Suggest experiment at 0300 UTC when low risk.

mike-eng: I'll open a short-lived playbook and run the repro. Tagging @sara-sre to perform node replacement. Will report back in <30m.

sara-sre: Starting cordon/drain on node hosting pod-7 now. ETA 12m.

olivia-cs: Thanks all — I'll update the Juno thread and ask for permission on the temporary scaling change. :thumbsup:
